# FluentCI

> FluentCI is an open-source, typed, programmable CI/CD tool for building, testing, and deploying locally or on runners. It combines a Rust CLI, WebAssembly engine, eight language SDKs, local Studio web/desktop app, and AT Protocol module registry.

Website: https://fluentci.io
Documentation: https://docs.fluentci.io
Documentation index: https://docs.fluentci.io/llms.txt
Repository: https://github.com/fluentci-io/fluentci
Engine: https://github.com/fluentci-io/fluentci-engine
Registry API: https://api.fluentci.io/xrpc
Module downloads: https://modules.fluentci.io

## Install and start

```sh
curl -fsSL https://cli.fluentci.io | sh
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
fluentci init --sdk clojurescript
fluentci run main hello
fluentci studio
```

The installer resolves the latest release and verifies checksums. FLUENTCI_VERSION
and FLUENTCI_INSTALL_DIR override its version and destination; set them on the
receiving sh process. Local execution and Studio require no account. Source
modules need their SDK compiler; precompiled Wasm still needs the tools used by
its jobs.

Homebrew: run `brew tap fluentci-io/tap` and `brew trust fluentci-io/tap`, then
`brew install fluentci-io/tap/fluentci`. The macOS desktop app is available with
`brew install --cask fluentci-io/tap/fluentci-studio`.

Nix: enable the public cache with `cachix use fluentci`, then install using
`nix profile install github:fluentci-io/fluentci`. Supported flake platforms are
x86_64-linux, aarch64-linux, and aarch64-darwin. The installation guide also covers
APT and DNF packages.

## SDKs, typed arguments, and native Wasm components

Supported SDKs: Rust, PureScript, ClojureScript, TypeScript, Python, Gleam, Elixir,
and ReScript. Wasm contains orchestration logic; host commands run through the
engine. Elixir compiles a CI DSL subset, not arbitrary BEAM programs.
ClojureScript checks shared .cljc source with Typed Clojure before compilation.

Extism core Wasm remains supported and is the default. Native WebAssembly
components run directly in Wasmtime with WASI Preview 2 and versioned WIT host
imports. Create a component in an existing workspace with:

```sh
fluentci modules add deploy --sdk purescript --runtime component
```

For a new workspace, use `fluentci init --sdk rust --runtime component`.
The corresponding [[modules]] field is runtime = "component". Artifact execution
detects the binary encoding; explicit component declarations reject core Wasm.
Component starters do not require an Extism guest compiler.

All eight SDKs can regenerate WIT and guest adapters from source contracts on
each build; developers do not have to maintain duplicate WIT. Rust uses parsed
signatures checked by compilation; JavaScript targets use compiler/type-checker
interfaces; Python uses annotations, dataclasses/TypedDicts, and aliases; Elixir
uses its executable DSL declarations. Unsupported or ambiguous types fail rather
than being guessed. Source comments provide descriptions. Rust/Elixir use
wit-bindgen, Python uses componentize-py, and JavaScript targets use ComponentizeJS.

Published function metadata includes descriptions, named arguments, argument
types, required/optional state, and return types. SDK inspection keeps metadata
synchronized on rebuild. Component arguments are validated against actual WIT.
Legacy Extism raw-text exports retain their ABI and do not automatically acquire
named flags. Component functions return values instead of using Extism input/output.

```sh
fluentci run main --help
fluentci run main hello --help
fluentci run main hello --name Tsiry
```

The final example assumes the Rust component starter's typed hello function.
Supported flags follow the inspected function contract. WIT identifiers and
corresponding CLI flags use kebab-case.

## Workspaces, workflows, and locking

Root fluentci.toml declares shared modules, services, and default steps. Module
sources can be SDK projects, precompiled .wasm files, HTTP(S) Wasm URLs, registry
packages, or Git repositories. Git sources support rev and subdir for monorepos.
Paths resolve from the configuration/project root.

Store multiple workflows in .fluentci/workflows/<id>.toml. Each has its own
name, description, environment, steps, and execution history, sharing root modules
and services:

```sh
fluentci workflows
fluentci workflows --steps --json
fluentci workflows release --steps
fluentci run --workflow release
```

CI events cover push, pull request, manual dispatch, and schedules with supported
branch/tag/path filters. These affect CI exports, not manual local triggering.
Studio offers a visual event composer. Exports support GitHub Actions, GitLab CI,
Azure Pipelines, CircleCI, Semaphore, and AWS CodeBuild. Provider limitations and
required external setup are documented in exports; trigger support differs.

Registry references use @handle/name with optional @version or @latest. Official
@fluentci.io/name modules can be referenced as name. Omitted/latest versions
initially resolve the latest stable release. Direct package or Wasm URL invocation
works without fluentci.toml:

```sh
fluentci run @tsiry-sandratraina.com/sccache@v0.1.0 --help
fluentci https://example.com/module.wasm --help
```

The URL is illustrative. fluentci.lock pins registry versions, artifact URLs,
SHA-256 checksums, and Git commits. `fluentci install` resolves dependencies;
`fluentci install --frozen-lockfile` enforces locks; `fluentci update` refreshes
resolutions deliberately. SDK dependency locks remain separate. `fluentci docs`
renders available module READMEs with Glow, honoring explicit readme_url or
repository/subdir discovery and locked Git sources where applicable.

## Native execution, services, and primitives

The engine compiles validated DAGs into indexed graphs with contiguous adjacency
arrays and incremental scheduling for ordinary dependency flows. JSON remains
readable interchange/debugging data, without a required internal graph round trip.
Native plans support typed matrices, dependencies, concurrency limits, retries,
conditions, allowed failures, outputs, artifacts, resources, caches, cancellation,
service probes, logs, and replayable event journals.

Composable primitives include filesystem operations, OS/CPU architecture detection,
SHA-256/SHA-512 text/file digests, SSH, SCP, SFTP, rsync, FTP, FTPS, and S3. rsync
is already a typed primitive backed by a native rsync 3+ client over SSH. Supported
client tools can be provisioned through the host package manager when installation
is enabled; remote tools must exist remotely. Credentials can reference task
environment variables.

The built-in POSIX process manager supervises background databases and other
services on macOS, Linux, FreeBSD, NetBSD, and OpenBSD. Define services in TOML,
Procfiles, or code. Backends include host, Nix, Devbox, Devenv, Pkgx, and Docker,
subject to platform/backend availability. Lifecycle support includes readiness,
health checks, dependencies, restart policies, logs, and cleanup. Commands include
fluentci up, ps, logs, restart, and down.

Pipeline environments also integrate Flox, Hermit, EnvHub, Pixi, and Mise. Local
and remote caches and OpenTelemetry tracing are supported. Environment providers
and their tools remain external dependencies.

## Registry, publishing, and authentication

Publishing uses FLUENTCI_ACCOUNT (handle or DID) and FLUENTCI_APP_PASSWORD.
`fluentci whoami` authenticates and shows account information; this flow has no
login command. Identity is remembered in ~/.fluentci/account.json without app
passwords or session tokens. Authentication can trigger background indexing of
public Tangled repositories into local SQLite for Studio clone suggestions.

Name, version, and license are required per module in fluentci.toml; version is
not read from package.version. Optional metadata includes description, repository,
subdir, logo, readme_url, topics, os, and arch. Interactive publishing prompts for
missing fields, offers license/platform completion, and lets users skip optional
fields. Non-interactive runs require explicit required metadata.

```sh
fluentci publish --module deploy
fluentci publish --name example --version 1.0.0 --license MIT --file dist/plugin.wasm
```

Publishing can build source, use --file, or validate --url to skip uploading.
External Wasm URLs must end in .wasm and return HTTP 200. Logo URLs must return
HTTP 200 with an image MIME type. Core Wasm and components are supported, with
inspected function/argument/return metadata.

The API verifies publisher-scoped service authentication, stores immutable Wasm
in S3-compatible storage, and returns its public URL and checksum. The CLI writes
an io.fluentci.plugin record to the publisher's PDS using the name-version key.
Package identity is publisher scoped. Canonical download paths follow
/handle/module/v<version>/module.wasm; /@handle paths remain compatible. Public
downloads use modules.fluentci.io.

The Gleam/Node XRPC API uses SQLite, FTS5, Drizzle Gleam bindings, and multiple
deduplicated Jetstream connections. Endpoints provide package search with RSQL
platform filters, lookup, paginated lists, and actor package feeds. The root
returns an API overview; /xrpc/_health is the health endpoint.

PDS updates can change descriptive metadata. Jetstream preserves published
artifact URL, SHA-256, and version, and ignores delete events. Download counters
are registry owned. HTTP 200 Wasm GETs through the proxy asynchronously record
deduplicated total/daily download counts without blocking the download response.

## Studio and module discovery

Studio runs in a browser or Tauri desktop app with native macOS window controls.
It manages projects/workflows, execution bars and stats, live auto-following logs,
job re-runs, span timelines, and a bottom status line. Git controls show/switch
branches and pull changes; workflows/local modules refresh after branch changes.
Quick search includes workflows and parent projects. Module suggestions distinguish
local and registry modules and show logos or placeholders.

The landing page offers dark/light themes and a slash-shortcut search modal.
Results include module identity, logo, description, author, and available download
counts. Official @fluentci.io modules display unqualified names. Module pages show
README Markdown with syntax highlighting, typed function Docs and function search,
usage examples, version/date, author, license, repository, topics/platform metadata,
and available weekly download history.

## Documentation

- [Installation](https://docs.fluentci.io/getting-started/installation/): CLI, package managers, Nix, and platforms.
- [Modules](https://docs.fluentci.io/guides/modules/): Local, URL, registry, and Git sources.
- [WebAssembly components](https://docs.fluentci.io/guides/components/): Automatic WIT generation, SDK toolchains, native imports, and supported types.
- [Typed arguments](https://docs.fluentci.io/guides/module-arguments/): Inspected signatures, flags, descriptions, and legacy compatibility.
- [Configuration](https://docs.fluentci.io/reference/configuration/): fluentci.toml, workflows, events, and services.
- [Lockfile](https://docs.fluentci.io/reference/lockfile/): Reproducible registry/Git resolutions.
- [Native plans](https://docs.fluentci.io/guides/native-plans/): Graph compilation, matrices, and scheduling.
- [Primitives](https://docs.fluentci.io/guides/primitives/): Files, host facts, digests, transfers, rsync, and provisioning.
- [Services](https://docs.fluentci.io/guides/services/): Built-in supervision and development environments.
- [CI exports](https://docs.fluentci.io/guides/ci/): Provider mappings, event support, and setup.
- [SDKs](https://docs.fluentci.io/sdks/): All eight language SDKs.
- [Studio](https://docs.fluentci.io/studio/): Projects, workflows, history, logs, and spans.
- [Publishing](https://docs.fluentci.io/registry/publishing/): Metadata, validation, uploads, and PDS records.
- [Authentication](https://docs.fluentci.io/registry/authentication/): Environment credentials, identity, and Tangled indexing.
- [Registry API](https://docs.fluentci.io/reference/registry-api/): XRPC queries, filters, and pagination.
- [CLI reference](https://docs.fluentci.io/reference/cli/): Unified CLI commands; engine-only commands are not automatically top-level commands.

## Module-owned dependencies and publisher profiles

A module root can contain fluentci-module.toml with publishing metadata, SDK/runtime,
and a dependencies table. Run fluentci add <reference> there to update declarations,
install verified Wasm into the Git-ignored fluentci_modules directory, and update
fluentci.lock. Paths, registry references, Wasm URLs, and Git monorepo subdirectories
are supported. Run fluentci install --frozen-lockfile in CI. Dependency aliases work
with fluentci run <alias> <function>. Native component dependencies use generated WIT
imports and type-checked composition; Extism dependencies use scoped SDK module calls.
The FluentCI WIT host package remains at 0.1.0.

Publisher pages at /:handle or /:did display avatar, display name, handle, exact module
count, filtering, and infinite loading. Author links go to these FluentCI profiles.

- [Module dependencies](https://docs.fluentci.io/guides/module-dependencies/): Manifests, add/install, locking, SDK imports and dependency calls.
